disposition_reason: Ineligible for the registered developmental association task. Age/region effects in alpha frequency and intrinsic timescales are descriptive cross-sectional relationships. Increasing their R², significance or effect magnitude would not establish a better biological estimate; the local participant-held-out prediction scorer introduces a different task.

source_paper.title: Developmental relationships between the human alpha rhythm and intrinsic neural timescales are dependent on neural hierarchy

evidence.locator: Methods: Participants, Signal Processing, Spectral Calculations, Spectral Parameterization; Figs. 2–4 and Tables 1–3
evidence.supports: Source population, spectral estimands and descriptive age/hierarchy regressions.

evidence.locator: Intended order of operations and dependencies
evidence.supports: Links source data and specifies spectrum, spectral-fit, statistics sequence with the author Lorentzian FOOOF fork.

evidence.locator: Parameter/QC loading; sensorimotor/association grouping; PAF/INT omnibus/region regressions; interaction model cells
evidence.supports: Source fit0 QC, grouped smoothing and participant/region aggregation preceding descriptive regressions.

evidence.locator: Lorentzian fit setup, PAF and INT extraction cells
evidence.supports: Author estimator conventions and dependency-sensitive spectral extraction.

evidence.locator: Source semantics and prospective repairs; Native scientific gates retained
evidence.supports: Local held-out prediction metric and train-only comparator are prospective; native spectral conventions remain unresolved.

target.description: Estimate peak alpha frequency and intrinsic timescale, then characterize age relationships and their dependence on sensorimotor versus association hierarchy.

dataset.description: Original resting ECoG release Zenodo 16954184, linked by the paper; author README links the associated concept record 16954183.

cohort.description: Thirteen cross-sectional epilepsy-monitoring participants, approximately ages 3–33, with variable coverage of six cortical regions.

split.description: Original age/hierarchy regressions use the observed clinical cohort; no paper prediction holdout is defined. Local participant-held-out PAF/INT errors constitute an extension.

inputs.description: Resting ECoG, participant age, cortical-region assignments and montage/channel information.

preprocessing.description: Paper preprocessing and Lorentzian spectral fitting are documented, but historical fork identity, knee-to-timescale conversion and paper 3–14 Hz versus code 2–14 Hz alpha selection require reconciliation.

metric.description: PAF, INT and their age/hierarchy regression coefficients, correlations and R² quantify associations. R² is explanatory fit here, not a protected prediction baseline.

aggregation.description: The author notebook pools eligible time rows within participant/region or context, then regresses participant summaries against log2 age; the interaction uses participant-region summaries.

comparison.primary_metric: No ordered performance metric for hierarchy-dependent developmental associations

published_baseline.description: Published regression R² and p values are association statistics, not algorithmic performance scores eligible for maximization.

reproduced_author_baseline.description: No authentic source spectral-to-statistics rerun is established. The local train-only region-mean predictor is not an author baseline.

minimum_effect.rationale: A larger age association or smaller p value does not supply a meaningful improvement in estimation accuracy.

uncertainty.method: No paper-win uncertainty rule applies to maximizing the descriptive associations.
uncertainty.independent_unit: Participant; regional and temporal measurements are nested.
uncertainty.rationale: Regional rows and overlapping spectral windows cannot provide independent participant replication.

paper_win_requires: Do not promote regression significance, fit R² or closeness to source PAF/INT tables into a superiority claim.
Keep participant-held-out prediction and the local same-region mean comparator as a separately labelled extension.
An estimation-method replacement would need independently justified targets and the same original evaluation; changing the cohort or split is not a paper win.

current_sota.description: No current-SOTA comparison was performed; biological findings and reconstruction agreement are not SOTA scores.

episode.improvement_loop: No active loop for maximizing developmental associations; native estimator reconciliation remains calibration work.
episode.candidate_freeze: Not applicable for this descriptive endpoint. A future predictive extension must freeze a separate contract.
episode.final_evaluation: The local score-heldout route cannot establish surpassing the source developmental finding.
episode.baseline_policy: Keep original association statistics, author reproduction and prospective predictor errors distinct.

blocking_issues: The source developmental finding has no ordered algorithmic success endpoint.
Historical spectral dependency and paper/code estimator discrepancies remain unresolved; native calibration is incomplete.

legacy.notes: Preserve the postfit statistics implementation and prospective participant-held-out scoring component. Neither a better train-only predictor comparison nor stronger age/hierarchy inference establishes a same-task paper victory.
